items.claim: The three-site recurrence of the quoted-objection construction is stated beside a byte tier label, but the 3-verse digit holds at the consonantal tier alone (byte tier returns 1 verse), and one closing pairing reaches past the run it is attached to.
items.evidence: Sweeping the row's own pointed splice אֲשֶׁר֙ אַתֶּ֣ם אֹֽמְרִ֔ים (oshb:Jer.33.10, byte) returns 1 verse at byte tier and 1 at accent_stripped, oshb:Jer.33.10 alone, while the consonantal tier returns 3 verses (oshb:Jer.32.36, oshb:Jer.32.43, oshb:Jer.33.10). The two earlier sites read אֲשֶׁ֣ר אַתֶּ֣ם אֹמְרִ֗ים (oshb:Jer.32.36, byte), a different pointed string that sweeps to 2 verses at byte tier by itself. The 3-verse digit and the third-and-last ordering are therefore both correct, but the recurrence carries no tier of its own while a byte label sits on the adjacent quote, and a recurrence claim owes its tier at write time. Same class, smaller: the closing splice עַל יְדֵ֥י מוֹנֶ֖ה אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.33.13, byte) is paired with a rendering whose subject, עֹ֣ד תַּעֲבֹ֧רְנָה הַצֹּ֛אן (oshb:Jer.33.13, byte), lies outside the splice. The substance verifies: both formulas are verse-initial and divine-mouthed, the second carrying the expanded title at oshb:Jer.33.12; the yet-again cohesion binding the pair is byte-true, עוֹד֮ יִשָּׁמַ֣ע בַּמָּקוֹם הַזֶּה֒ (oshb:Jer.33.10, byte) against יְהוָ֣ה צְבָאוֹת֒ ע֞וֹד יִֽהְיֶ֣ה (oshb:Jer.33.12, byte); and the span's mark inventory is disclosed in full (2 setumah entries in span at oshb:Jer.33.11 and oshb:Jer.33.13, 2 paseq entries at oshb:Jer.33.10 and oshb:Jer.33.12, single-witness WLC, count-only; no variant note anywhere in the span).

items.claim: The internal-seam argument misplaces what the formula at 33:17 governs, and the structured signal key files the days-are-coming formula under the date-frame family, where the byte-swept census does not put it.
items.evidence: כִּי כֹ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה לֹֽא יִכָּרֵ֣ת (oshb:Jer.33.17, byte) is a ki-subordinated formula introducing the David-throne guarantee, not a fresh onset; the turn to the priesthood falls one verse later at וְלַכֹּהֲנִים֙ הַלְוִיִּ֔ם לֹֽא יִכָּרֵ֥ת (oshb:Jer.33.18, byte), which opens on a plain waw and carries no formula at all. Both witnesses agree, “David will never lack a man to sit on the throne of the house of Israel” (web:Jer.33.17). The row states twice, in the rationale and again in the rejected alternative, that the 33:17 formula is where the guarantee turns from David's throne to the Levitical altar; that is byte-false, so the rival reading being declined is described at the wrong verse and under a device that is not there. Second defect: the signal key files הִנֵּ֛ה יָמִ֥ים בָּאִ֖ים (oshb:Jer.33.14, byte) under the date-frame family, but the book's date and reign header object holds 19 classified candidate sites and oshb:Jer.33.14 is not among them; this formula sweeps as a temporal prophetic shape at 5 verses byte tier (oshb:Jer.9.24 = web:Jer.9.25, oshb:Jer.31.27, oshb:Jer.31.31, oshb:Jer.31.38, oshb:Jer.33.14) and 15 verses at the consonantal tier. The one-unit reading of 33:14-18 survives both defects; the driver description and the machine-readable key do not. Minor: the paseq inside the span at oshb:Jer.33.16 goes undisclosed while that same verse's setumah is cited. The repeated-verb disclosure is otherwise honest, the two forms being quoted separately and byte-distinctly at oshb:Jer.33.17 and oshb:Jer.33.18.

items.claim: The closing comparison at 33:22 is named as a second analogy from the day-night covenant, but the bytes draw it from the uncountable host of heaven and the immeasurable sand of the sea.
items.evidence: oshb:Jer.33.22 opens אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא יִסָּפֵר֙ צְבָ֣א הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְלֹ֥א יִמַּ֖ד ח֣וֹל הַיָּ֑ם (oshb:Jer.33.22, byte) before the apodosis כֵּ֣ן אַרְבֶּ֗ה אֶת זֶ֨רַע֙ דָּוִ֣ד עַבְדִּ֔י (oshb:Jer.33.22, byte) that the row splices; the comparandum is creation order, not the covenant of oshb:Jer.33.20 and oshb:Jer.33.21, and the words carrying it sit entirely outside the splice, so the mischaracterisation is invisible from the quoted run alone. WEB stands with the pointed text, “As the army of the sky can’t be counted, and the sand of the sea can’t be measured” (web:Jer.33.22). Second, same class: the conditional splice stops at בְּרִיתִ֣י (oshb:Jer.33.20, byte) while its paired rendering runs on through the night covenant, that is past הַיּ֔וֹם וְאֶת בְּרִיתִ֖י הַלָּ֑יְלָה (oshb:Jer.33.20, byte). The seam itself is sound: both bounding formulas are verse-initial members of the word-event set (oshb:Jer.33.19, oshb:Jer.33.23), the plene infinitive spelling at oshb:Jer.33.19 against the defective spelling at oshb:Jer.33.23 is reproduced byte-exactly, no addressee or frame-owner change falls inside the span, and mark disclosure is complete for it (1 setumah in span at oshb:Jer.33.22, plus the preceding close at oshb:Jer.33.18; single-witness WLC; no paseq and no variant note in the span).

items.claim: The declared false positive on the in-field variant disclosure is refuted: the form-exact recurrence sweep (2 verses at byte tier) lands on the qere at 1 of its 2 sites, and the field carrying that sweep gives no variant disclosure.
items.evidence: The digit is confirmed independently: the quoted clause sweeps to exactly 2 verses at byte tier, oshb:Jer.32.44 and oshb:Jer.33.26, and to the same 2 at the consonantal tier. But at oshb:Jer.33.26 the matched token is the qere, the bytes reading כִּֽי אשוב אָשִׁ֥יב אֶת שְׁבוּתָ֖ם (oshb:Jer.33.26, byte), the unpointed ketiv standing immediately before the pointed qere, while oshb:Jer.32.44 carries no variant note at all. A form-exact recurrence asserted across one marked and one unmarked site, in the single field that omits the ketiv and qere disclosure the rest of the row carries, is the guarded hazard rather than a false positive: the marks must be read before a form-exact claim in a marked verse, and here they were read in one field and not in the other. Adjacent texture also left undisclosed: the near variant אָשִׁ֧יב אֶת שְׁבוּת הָאָ֛רֶץ (oshb:Jer.33.11, byte) stands fifteen verses earlier, the wider construction sweeping to 4 verses at the consonantal tier (oshb:Jer.32.44, oshb:Jer.33.11, oshb:Jer.33.26, oshb:Jer.49.6). Everything else verifies: oshb:Jer.33.23 is indeed the fourth verse-initial word-event onset of this two-chapter block after oshb:Jer.32.26, oshb:Jer.33.1 and oshb:Jer.33.19; the ketiv and qere forms named in the rationale are byte-exact; and mark disclosure is complete for the span (2 setumah entries in span at oshb:Jer.33.24 and oshb:Jer.33.26, plus the preceding close at oshb:Jer.33.22; single-witness WLC).

items.claim: All 8 pointed splices reach byte tier at their cited coordinates and every device claim holds: the header form with its aleph-lamed spelling, the royal name family, the vav-prefixed funeral cry (sweep: 2 verses book-wide), the siege inclusio and the full span mark inventory.
items.evidence: oshb:Jer.34.1 opens הַדָּבָ֛ר אֲשֶׁר הָיָ֥ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ מֵאֵ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.34.1, byte) with the aleph-lamed preposition, the prose-sermon superscription shape and not the one-site ayin-lamed variant standing elsewhere in the book; that seven-word header sweeps to 4 verses at byte tier (oshb:Jer.21.1, oshb:Jer.34.1, oshb:Jer.34.8, oshb:Jer.35.1) and 10 at accent_stripped, so the string quoted here is byte-identical with the headers opening the two following units. The royal name in that same verse is וּנְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֣ר (oshb:Jer.34.1, byte), the nun-resh spelling of the 29-verse family, and no name-form digit is hung on it. The funeral cry is quoted in its attested shape וְה֥וֹי אָד֖וֹן יִסְפְּדוּ לָ֑ךְ (oshb:Jer.34.5, byte); that vav-prefixed form sweeps to 2 verses book-wide at byte tier (oshb:Jer.22.18, oshb:Jer.34.5) and is invisible to a bare-token sweep, and the row role-splits it from the woe onsets, the day-alas cry and the sword apostrophe, 0 of which fall in the span. The closing siege notice בָּבֶ֗ל נִלְחָמִים֙ עַל (oshb:Jer.34.7, byte) answers נִלְחָמִ֧ים עַל יְרוּשָׁלִַ֛ם (oshb:Jer.34.1, byte), a byte-true inclusio bracketing the row. Mark disclosure is complete and correctly typed, petuchah never conflated with setumah: setumah at oshb:Jer.34.5 in span and at oshb:Jer.33.26 preceding, petuchah closing at oshb:Jer.34.7, paseq count-only at oshb:Jer.34.1 (single-witness WLC, weak corroboration in the Prophets), with no variant note anywhere in the span. The parent turns at 34:1 with no straddle, and all 8 pointed splices in the row reach byte tier at the refs they cite. One cosmetic lapse only, not a defect of substance: the byte tier label is attached to bare coordinates in the device field where no run is quoted.

items.claim: A byte-true release-term chain runs across this row's own closing seam and is disclosed in neither field.
items.evidence: The release noun stands inside this span at לִקְרֹ֥א לָהֶ֖ם דְּרֽוֹר (oshb:Jer.34.8, byte) and then twice past the seam at oshb:Jer.34.15 and oshb:Jer.34.17; the consonantal sweep returns 3 verses book-wide and all 3 sit in this chapter, so the term is attested on both sides of the cut. A byte-true device straddling a row's own seam argues continuity against the cut unless disclosed, and the row names it in neither of its prose fields, although the covenant it narrates is precisely the release that term denotes. The cut itself survives the challenge: oshb:Jer.34.12 is a verse-initial member of the word-event set, so a tier-1 onset genuinely falls there. Everything else verifies byte-exactly: oshb:Jer.34.8 carries the same seven-word superscription header as oshb:Jer.34.1 and oshb:Jer.35.1 (sweep: 4 verses at byte tier); the closing variant pair is quoted as the bytes have it, שִׁלְּח֖וּ חָפְשִׁ֑ים (oshb:Jer.34.11, byte), unpointed ketiv before pointed qere; and mark disclosure is complete and typed, petuchah at oshb:Jer.34.7 preceding and setumah closing at oshb:Jer.34.11 (single-witness WLC), the variant note at that same coordinate kept as a separate object from the mark.

items.claim: The structured signal key classifies the 34:12 word-event formula as non-initial, which the verse bytes and the book-wide census both contradict, and the parashah citations doing pivot work in the rationale stand there without their witness disclosure.
items.evidence: oshb:Jer.34.12 is a whole verse of 8 words opening on the formula itself, וַיְהִ֤י דְבַר יְהוָה֙ אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ מֵאֵ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.34.12, byte), so the formula is verse-initial. The byte-swept word-event census carries this verse among the 21 sites of that shape and records 20 of them verse-initial with exactly 1 non-initial site, which lies elsewhere in the book; filing this one as non-initial therefore asserts a second non-initial site against a byte-proven single-site fact, in the machine-readable field, and it contradicts the row's own rationale, which calls the formula the opening of the reply and quotes the full verse. Second: the rationale places the setumah at oshb:Jer.34.16 at the recitation-to-sentence pivot and a petuchah at the row's close, both without the single-witness naming this layer requires on every citation, both inside the field carrying the boundary argument, and with the mark set at precisely the pivot the row declines to cut; the disclosure appears only in the device field. Third: the release-term chain reaching this span from oshb:Jer.34.8 (sweep: 3 verses, all in this chapter) crosses the row's own opening seam undisclosed. What does verify: both variant pairs are byte-exact, לזועה לְזַעֲוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.34.17, byte) and the front-seam note at oshb:Jer.34.11; the covenant-ritual vocabulary אֲשֶׁ֥ר כָּרְת֖וּ לְפָנָ֑י הָעֵ֨גֶל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר (oshb:Jer.34.18, byte) sits where claimed; the frame owner is the same divine mouth on both sides of oshb:Jer.34.17, so the decision not to cut at the therefore-clause is itself sound; and the span is 11 verses of a 22-verse chapter, so no whole-chapter calibration applies.

items.claim: Two byte-checkable naming lapses: the armies fled from are Chaldean in both witnesses rather than Babylonian, and the ancestor whose charge the unit turns on stands in two attested spellings inside this span, undisclosed.
items.evidence: oshb:Jer.35.11 reads מִפְּנֵי֙ חֵ֣יל הַכַּשְׂדִּ֔ים וּמִפְּנֵ֖י חֵ֣יל אֲרָ֑ם (oshb:Jer.35.11, byte); the Babylon token stands once in that verse (1 occurrence), inside the royal title נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֥ר מֶֽלֶךְ בָּבֶל֮ (oshb:Jer.35.11, byte), and the Babylon token, the directional form and the Chaldeans token are kept as separate count objects, so naming the armies Babylonian blends two of them at the one place in the span where the distinction is visible. WEB stands with the pointed text, “for fear of the army of the Chaldeans, and for fear of the army of the Syrians” (web:Jer.35.11). Second: the ancestor is named inside this span in two attested spellings, the short יוֹנָדָ֨ב (oshb:Jer.35.6, byte), which sweeps to 3 verses at the consonantal tier, and the long יְהוֹנָדָ֤ב (oshb:Jer.35.8, byte), which sweeps to 4, both confined to this chapter; the row quotes the short form alone and leaves the variance unmentioned, although the whole unit rests on his charge. Neither lapse moves a boundary. The rest verifies: oshb:Jer.35.1 carries the byte-identical seven-word superscription header shared with oshb:Jer.34.1 and oshb:Jer.34.8 (sweep: 4 verses at byte tier); the days-of-Jehoiakim setting is correctly not claimed as a member of the 19-site date and reign header object, and no date key is assigned to it; the wine vocabulary is the yayin lexeme at oshb:Jer.35.2, oshb:Jer.35.5 and oshb:Jer.35.6, with no blending into the distinct new-wine noun that stands elsewhere in the book; oshb:Jer.35.12 is a verse-initial word-event onset closing the span; and the span's marked coordinates are exactly 2, the petuchah closing oshb:Jer.35.11 and the count-only paseq at oshb:Jer.35.5, with the petuchah at oshb:Jer.34.22 disclosed as the preceding close (single-witness WLC).
